sources.entry: GameAP - Game Administration Panel for managing game servers on Linux and Windows. (Demo, Source Code, Clients) MIT Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: GameAP is a free, open-source web panel for managing and deploying game servers, with a Go single-binary panel and per-node daemon agents.
summary.what_it_does: The panel provides a browser UI, REST API and WebSocket endpoint for real-time task output, console streams and metrics, storing data in PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, SQLite, or an in-memory database for testing. Each node runs a GameAP Daemon agent that connects to the panel over a long-lived gRPC bidirectional stream secured with TLS or mTLS, and controls game server processes (start, stop, monitor, configure). The README describes TLS termination with three certificate sources, including built-in Let's Encrypt (ACME) with http-01 or dns-01 (Cloudflare) challenges. Configuration is entirely through environment variables, covering caching (memory, Redis, Postgres), file storage (local or S3), CAPTCHA on login, HTTP security headers, and a WebAssembly plugin system with fine-grained capability limits. Docker and Docker Compose are offered as a quick start, and gameapctl is mentioned as a helper CLI.
use_cases: manage multiple game servers from a web panel
deploy and control game server processes on remote nodes
run a game hosting panel for customers
obtain automatic Let's Encrypt certificates for a control panel
add plugins to a game server admin panel
single sign-on from a billing system into a customer's panel
how_to_run: docker run -d -p 8025:8025 -e DATABASE_DRIVER=sqlite -e DATABASE_URL=file:/db.sqlite?_busy_timeout=5000&_journal_mode=WAL&cache=shared -e ENCRYPTION_KEY=your-secret-key -e AUTH_SECRET=your-auth-secret gameap/gameap:latest
notable: Single binary panel with no pre-installed dependencies required
Built-in Let's Encrypt client with hot-swapped certificates, no certbot or nginx needed
Node agent (daemon) over a single gRPC stream with TLS/mTLS
WebAssembly plugin system with per-plugin permission grants and rate limits
Multi-instance support with Redis pub/sub and shared S3 storage
caveats: In-memory database is for testing only and loses data on restart
Multi-instance http-01 ACME needs sticky sessions at the load balancer; dns-01 is recommended
Only Cloudflare is named as a built-in ACME DNS provider; other providers are said to be planned
